faq.a: Gregor Mendel was a monk and scientist in Brno who bred about 28,000 pea plants between 1856 and 1863. He showed that traits are passed on by units we now call genes, in predictable ratios.

He published in a small local journal, used maths that most biologists then did not use, and nobody yet knew about chromosomes. In 1900 Hugo de Vries, Carl Correns and Erich von Tschermak rediscovered it.

faq.q: What is the chromosome theory of inheritance?
faq.a: In 1902 and 1903 Walter Sutton and Theodor Boveri showed that chromosomes behave in meiosis just like Mendel's units, so genes must be carried on chromosomes.
asks: Tell me about genes on chromosomes

faq.a: James Watson and Francis Crick proposed it in 1953, using X-ray images by Rosalind Franklin and Raymond Gosling and data from Maurice Wilkins.
asks: Tell me about the double helix

faq.q: What was the Human Genome Project?
faq.a: An international project, from 1990 to 2003, that read the order of about 3 billion DNA bases in human chromosomes. It helps doctors find genes linked to diseases.
asks: Tell me about the human genome

facts: Mendel presented his pea results in Brno in 1865 and published them in 1866.
The Human Genome Project was declared complete in 2003.
